title: Tata Power announces US$ 1.5 billion Mumbai grid expansion for data centers
key_facts: Tata Power, part of India's Tata Group, announced a Rs 15,000 crore (about US$1.5 billion) plan to upgrade and expand Mumbai's power grid for data centers.
It is upgrading its 110 kV and 220 kV network and building new receiving stations and a 400 kV transmission ring.
It reports a pipeline of over 2.8 GW across renewables, transmission and distribution, and 29 active workstreams with 18 data center operators.
India's power ministry, using CEA estimates, projects AI-led data centers could add about 26.3 GW of demand by FY2031-32.
quote_evidence: Tata Power, a vertically integrated power company and part of the Tata Group, India's largest multinational business conglomerate, has announced a ₹15,000 crore (~US$ 1.5 billion) Mumbai grid upgradation and expansion plan to cater to the digital infrastructure being developed in the region.
Tata Power says that it has a diversified opportunity pipeline of over 2.8 GW spanning renewable energy, transmission and distribution opportunities.
why_it_matters_hint: Data center growth is forcing utilities in big cities to rebuild their grids.
notes: Company press release relayed by W.Media; figures are company claims.
